title: The Tylenol Murders, Part I
summary: Hosts Josh and Chuck open with tour announcements and banter about 1982 (movies, news events), then cover the 1982 Chicago Tylenol murders: the deaths of seven people beginning September 29, 1982 (the transcript's "two" likely refers to 1982) after extra-strength Tylenol capsules laced with potassium cyanide. They walk through each victim, the medical examiner's discovery of cyanide, how cyanide kills, the investigation and Chicago Tylenol Task Force, the public warnings, copycat tamperings (Excedrin with mercuric chloride, Visine with acid, ballpark hot dog scare), and the "mad poisoner" theory. Part one ends mid-October with a near-miss at a family gathering; part two is promised.
topics: Stuff You Should Know Tylenol Part I

segments.title: Live tour announcement
segments.summary: Hosts announce their upcoming live tour dates and ticket sale timing.

segments.title: Opening banter and 1982 context
segments.summary: Hosts chat about movies and recall the news of 1982, including Air Florida Flight 90, Wayne Williams' conviction, and the Pan Am crash.

segments.title: What Tylenol was and the first death
segments.summary: Explanation of Tylenol (Thailand All) as the dominant pain reliever, and the death of 12-year-old Mary Anne Kellerman after taking an extra-strength capsule on September 29.

segments.title: Adam Janus and Mary Reiner deaths
segments.summary: Adam Janus dies of an apparent heart attack after taking Tylenol for chest pains; later that day Mary Reiner dies after taking Tylenol for dizziness.

segments.title: Mary McFarland and the Janus family deaths
segments.summary: Mary McFarland collapses at an Illinois Bell store; Stanley and Teresa Janus die at Adam's home after taking Tylenol. Paula Prince is found dead days later.

segments.title: Mid-episode break
segments.summary: Short ad break after the seven deaths are summarized.

segments.title: Discovery of cyanide and how cyanide kills
segments.summary: Medical examiner Michael Schaefer finds potassium cyanide in the capsules. The hosts explain how cyanide disrupts cytochrome c oxidase and causes rapid death, along with symptoms like bright red skin and almond smell.

segments.title: Linking the deaths and public warning
segments.summary: Fire captain Philip Capitelli and public health nurse Helen Jensen push to connect the deaths. Cook County deputy chief medical examiner Edmund Donohue issues a press conference telling people to stop taking Tylenol, followed by Mayor Jane Byrne's warnings.

segments.title: Copycat tampering and hoaxes
segments.summary: Copycat tampering incidents occur nationwide, including Excedrin with mercuric chloride and Visine with acid. A scare over ballpark hot dogs and Halloween candy tampering is discussed.

segments.title: Task force, supply chain, and mad poisoner theory
segments.summary: The five investigations are merged into the Tylenol task force. Investigators trace the tainting to stores rather than the factory, and the mad poisoner theory is adopted after Johnson & Johnson's samples test pure.

segments.title: Mid-October bottle and part two tease
segments.summary: Another tainted bottle purchased September 29 is found, a woman is nearly poisoned at a family gathering, and the hosts promote part two and the show's contact info.
